ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circle with F as the center, and A, B, C are on the circle; AB is the chord on the left side, and BC is the slanted chord above. Point D is on chord AB, and the line segment FD from the center F to D is perpendicular to AB, with a right-angle mark in the figure. Point E is on chord BC, and the line segment FE from the center F to E is perpendicular to BC, also with a right-angle mark. Reasoning: The problem gives AB ≅ BC, so these two chords are congruent in the same circle. According to congruent chords in the same circle having equal distances to the center, DF = FE. It is also given that DF = 3x - 7, FE = x + 9, therefore 3x - 7 = x + 9. Solving gives 2x = 16, so x = 8.

method.method_draft: Use a proof-derived route rather than quoting the equidistant chord theorem directly. From the diagram, FD is perpendicular to AB at D and FE is perpendicular to BC at E. Since F is the center, a perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects that chord, so D is the midpoint of AB and E is the midpoint of BC. From the text AB ≅ BC, their halves are equal, so DB = EB. Add/consider segment FB; triangles FDB and FEB are right triangles sharing hypotenuse FB, with one corresponding leg DB = EB. By HL congruence or by the Pythagorean theorem, the remaining legs are equal, so DF = FE. Substitute 3x - 7 = x + 9 and solve x = 8.
